title: Propolis Preparation and Chemical Analysis
author: Gamal Mehaisen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s7hehj6

steps.title: Extract Propolis
steps.instruction: Extract the collected propolis using 70% ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Extract for one week with 70% ethanol at room temperature.

steps.title: Filter and Concentrate Extract
steps.instruction: Filter the propolis extract and remove the solvent.

substeps.instruction: Remove ethanol using a vacuum evaporator at 50°C.

steps.title: Store Extracted Propolis
steps.instruction: Store the resulting propolis powder in a dark bottle at 4°C until use.

steps.title: Perform DPPH Free Radical Scavenging Assay
steps.instruction: Measure the free radical scavenging activity of the propolis extract.

substeps.instruction: Mix extracted propolis at concentrations of 25 to 75 μg/mL with a 0.1 mM solution of 1,1-diphenyl-2-picryl-hydrazil (DPPH) in methanol.
Shake the mixtures vigorously and allow them to stand at room temperature for 30 min.
Measure the absorbance of the reactions using an automatic spectrophotometer at 517 nm.

steps.title: Analyze Propolis via HPLC
steps.instruction: Analyze the phenolic acids and flavonoid contents using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC).

substeps.instruction: Set the HPLC (Agilent 1260 Infinity Series) to 25°C using a Quaternary pump and a Zorbax Eclipse plus C18 column (150 mm × 4.6 mm internal diameters, 5 μm particle).
Perform a ternary linear elution profile using a gradient of water in 0.2% H3PO4 (v/v), methanol, and acetonitrile.
Set the variable wavelength detector (VWD) to 284 nm.
